This well lies beneath the root of Yggdrasil that extends into Asgard. The Aesir are said to hold council here, and it takes its name from one of the figures that are said to come from it, the Norns.
This eagle hangs out between the eyes of a hawk at the top of Yggdrasil. His pastimes include sending Ratatosk to deliver insults and gossip to Nidhogg.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about everyone's favorite world tree. No, not the furry pen and paper RPG which features the Zi Ri, a race of "immortal hermaphrodite dragons," Yggdrasil. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this Norse god, who was apparently really handsome, but also useless, because at councils he would just say "Let others decide" if his fellow hostage Mimir were not present.
Because Hoenir was useless and annoying, Mimir was killed. This body part of his was sent back to the Aesir, and was eventually kept by Odin.
Hoenir survives this apocalyptic battle of Norse mythology, and gains the gift of prophecy. Odin and Thor, along with many other gods, die during it.

bonuses.leadin: Along with Odin and Lodurr, this deity helped create the first humans Ask and Embla by giving them reason. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these things, one of which was destroyed by Saint Boniface (BAH-nif-us). Ratatoskr (RAT-uh-tosk-ur) carried messages on a mythical one of these objects.
This chief god of the Norse pantheon hanged himself on the world tree Yggdrasil (IG-drus-il) for nine days in order to understand the runes.
Yggdrasil is attested in the Völuspá (VOO-loosh-poh) section of this Old Norse literary work. Much of this originally untitled work was preserved in the Codex Regius.

bonuses.leadin: In western Norway, ale was poured over the Warden example of these things as part of a yearly festival. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this country, whose myths tell of the Coraniaid invasion. A king of this country gave his neighbor a magic cauldron to make up for an unfortunate incident of horse mutilation.
Lludd and Llefelys bury two of these beings underneath Snowdonia after catching them in a pit filled with mead. In a similar tale, Susano'o gets one of these creatures drunk to defeat it.
King Lludd was known for having a hand made out of this substance. It is common knowledge that a werewolf may be killed by shooting it with a bullet molded from this precious metal.

bonuses.leadin: A king of this country genocided his enemies by crushing up some insects, soaking them in water, and spraying everybody with the resulting bioweapon. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this jackal-headed Egyptian god who judged whether souls were worthy to enter the realm of the dead.
To judge the dead, Anubis utilized a scale and a feather named for this goddess of truth and balance.
The feather of Ma'at was weighed against this vital organ, which the Egyptians considered the seat of the soul. If weighed-down with wrongdoing, this organ would be devoured by Ammit.

bonuses.leadin: By the time of the Middle Kingdom, this god had been supplanted by Osiris as lord of the underworld. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name this man, who cheats death by binding Thanatos in his own chains. Eventually, he is condemned to push a boulder up a hill forever in Tartarus.
Sisyphus legendarily founded this city, which hosted non-Olympic "Games" named for the isthmus connecting the Peloponnese to the rest of Greece.

In some traditions, Sisyphus was the father of this man because he assaulted Anticlea as revenge for Autolycus stealing his cattle. This "man of many turns" is first recognized in his home kingdom by the wet nurse Eurycleia.

bonuses.leadin: This man assaults his niece Tyro to take revenge on his brother Salmoneus. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this hero who escaped the destruction of Troy and established the city of Rome after defeating Turnus and the Rutulians in battle. He also visited his father Anchises in the underworld.

In order to reach the underworld, Aeneas was required to present this mythological branch to Persephone as a gift. After Aeneas acquired this object, a new one grew in its place to foreshadow his successful journey.
This woman advised Aeneas in his journey to the underworld. According to legend, she wrote her prophecies on oak leaves and offered nine books of them to Tarquinius.

bonuses.leadin: This man's son pointed out that his people were eating the very tables they were dining on, causing him to realize that his journey had ended. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this god of wine and agriculture.
As a youth, Dionysus was kidnapped for ransom. After learning who he was, the sailors leaped into the sea, after which Dionysus turned them into these aquatic animals.
Upon being accepted as part of the pantheon, Dionysus needed a place to sit. This goddess of the hearth willingly gave up her throne.

bonuses.leadin: He was birthed from his father's thigh after his mother was incinerated. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this Hindu god of beginnings.

So large were the pasturelands of Atlantis that these large animals thrived. When Shiva decapitated Ganesha his was replaced with a head of one of these animals, which allowed Ganesha to later throw a tusk at the moon.

Ganesha and his six headed brother Skanda were the sons of this woman. In one account, this woman fashioned Ganesha from the dirt on her skin, and she is the reincarnation of Shiva's first consort, Sati.

bonuses.leadin: The moon is forced to wax and wane as a punishment for laughing at this god after his stomach burst from excessive indulgence of candy. For 10 points each:

parts.text: The roots of a mountain along with other things like the sinews of a bear, a woman's beard, and breath of a fish are all components of this mythological object that holds down Fenrir.
This mythological mountain is reportedly the home of the chief of the gods Brahma in Hindu myth systems. It is sacred to Jains as well and you might wanna know Angkor Wat was designed to imitate it.
During the Titanomachy, Zeus et al. had to fight the titans, who were basing their siege from this mountain, located in present day Lamia.

bonuses.leadin: Identify the following about mythological mountains, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Aphrodite turned this athlete into a lion after she desecrated this goddess's temple. Earlier, this woman had killed two centaurs who assaulted her and was also the first to wound the Calydonian boar.
This mortal weaver's hubris led Athena to challenge her weaving skills in a contest. Upon losing that contest, Athena turned this woman into a spider so that she could weave forever.

After this woman's husband, Cadmus, killed a sacred dragon, they were both transformed into serpents. This woman's cursed necklace, given to her by Athena and Hephaestus, may have been the cause of that misfortune.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, name some Greeks that got turned into various animals.

parts.text: This man had a lock of purple hair that made him invulnerable until it was cut by Scylla when Eros made Scylla fall in love with Minos, the king of Athens who was waging war against this King of Megara.
This elderly Phrygian couple was turned into oak and linden trees when they showed hospitality to Zeus and Hermes. Unlike their neighbors, they didn't drown in a flood.
Perdix, who was transformed into a partridge, was nearly killed by this man, the constructor of the Labyrinth and father Icarus.

bonuses.leadin: Name these characters discussed in Book VIII of Ovid's Metamorphoses, for ten points each.

parts.text: Name this hero from Greek myth who received a golden bridle from Athena after sleeping in her temple on advice from the seer Polyeidus.
Bellerophon slew this fire-breathing monster with the head of a lion, the body of a goat, and the tail of a snake by flying at it on Pegasus and ramming a lead block down its throat.
Bellerophon got cocky about having slain the Chimera and tried to fly to this mountain home of the Greek gods, but Zeus sent a gadfly to sting Pegasus, which caused him to fall.

bonuses.leadin: When this figure refused to sleep with the queen of Tiryns, she accused him of attempted rape. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this horse who kills a lion during the first of seven trials in the course of defeating Div-e-Sepid ("DEEV-eh-seh-PEED"). This horse perishes alongside his master due to Shaghad's treachery.

This hero tames Rakhsh and continually rescues Kay Kavus ("kai ka-VOOSE"). This hero meets Princess Tahmina when Rakhsh disappears on a hunting trip, and belatedly recognizes the bracelet he left with Tahmina after breaking a hero's back.
Rakhsh and Rostam appear in this national epic of Iran, written by Ferdowsi.

bonuses.leadin: This horse is described with a body "bright and dappled as though flecked with petals of red roses on saffron," and a price of "Iran itself." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this crippled Greek god of metalworking.
Hephaestus created this Greek god's winged helmet and sandals. This trickster god later lent those sandals to Perseus.
Hephaestus also created this first woman in Greek mythology. Because her namesake box was opened, this woman released evils into the world.

bonuses.leadin: This god was thrown off of Mount Olympus by his mother because of his deformity. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Freya slept with a number of these figures in exchange for the necklace Brisingamen, while a group of them known as the Sons of Ivaldi forged the spear Gungnir. These diminutive figures are often conflated with dark elves.
Female figures called the Norns hang out under the roots of Yggdrasil near the Well of Urdr, and are roughly analogous to these Greek figures, three women known as Clotho, Lachesis, and Atropos.

These deceased warriors are brought by valkyries to Valhalla, where they drink mead produced by the goat Heidrun and eat from the regenerating beast Saehrimnir in between bouts of fighting each other.

bonuses.leadin: Identify some groups from Norse myth which are neither the Aesir nor the Vanir, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Consisting of Clotho, Lachesis ("luh-KEE-sis"), and Atropos ("AT-row-pos"), these three control the threads that make up people's lives. Even Zeus knows to give this group a wide berth.

This group went after Orestes for fratricide, but he was eventually found innocent of the charges. Made up of Megaera ("muh-GARE-uh"), Tisiphone ("tih-SIFF-uh-nee"), and Alecto ("uh-LECK-toe"), these three pursue sinners who are not punished.

This group consists of Aello ("AIL-oh"), Celaeno ("kuh-LANE-oh"), and Ocypete ("oh-KIE-pet-ee"). These winged females with sharp talons torment people, and their actions almost made Phineus starve to death, until they were driven off. Their name is now synonymous with a woman who is evil.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, name these female groups from Greek myth that one should make great effort not to anger:

parts.text: Name this Aesir goddess whose "second sorrow" was her husband's death during Ragnarok at the jaws of the wolf Fenrir.
Frigg's husband was this god, who rode the eight-legged steed Sleipnir and was accompanied by the ravens Huginn and Muninn. He was also the All-Father and chief god of the Norse pantheon.
Frigg's first sorrow was the death of her son Baldr, who was killed by a mistletoe dart flung by this member of the Aesir. Baldr was eventually avenged when Vali slew this blind son of Odin.

bonuses.leadin: This figure is often identified with the infrequently attested goddess Hlin. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this subject of a Greek tragedy that, after killing his father Laius and sleeping with his mother Jocasta, fulfills a prophecy and gouges his own eyes out.
This Greek tragedian wrote a cycle of plays about Oedipus, as well as Ajax, Philoctetes, and The Women of Trachis.
This other Sophocles play concerns Oreste's sister and her quest to ruin Clytemnestra and Aegithus after they murdered her father Agamemnon.

bonuses.leadin: He gives an answer of "Man" to the sphinx's riddle and has a daughter named Antigone. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this type of journey whose process leads to or destination is something of spiritual or religious significance.

Hindus on the Kumbh Mela pilgrimage journey to holy examples of these geographical features. Christians often travel to the feature of this type where Namaan was cured of leprosy and where the Holy Spirit proclaimed Jesus to be the only son of God.

Pilgrimage to this Spanish church was super popular in the Middle Ages. Travelers from France look for shells that mark the most popular routes towards this cathedral, which holds the bones of its namesake saint.

bonuses.leadin: Popular examples of these trips include the one to Lourdes and the hajj. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this characteristic. A deity who was responsible for conferring this attribute on others served as the cupbearer to the gods prior to Ganymede.
This hero gains eternal youth by marrying Hebe after he gains immortality. While a mortal, this hero completed twelve labors as penance for killing his first wife and children.
This object granted its user eternal youth. This cursed object was created by Haephestus to get revenge on Aphrodite by bringing misfortune on her descendants through this object's namesake.

bonuses.leadin: After Eos forgets to ask Zeus to give this characteristic to her lover Tithonus, he is turned into a cricket. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this animal-human hybrid from Greek mythology, for which Daedalus [DED-ah-lus] built a maze-like labyrinth.
This Athenian hero ventured into the Labyrinth to slay the Minotaur. This hero's father committed suicide when this hero forgot to switch his sails from black to white upon returning to Athens.
This princess gave Theseus a ball of string to keep him from getting lost in the Labyrinth. According to some sources, she became the consort of Dionysus after being abandoned by Theseus.

bonuses.leadin: Seven boys and seven girls were regularly sent to be used as sacrifices to this creature. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name this city, conquered by the Greeks with the aid of a large wooden horse.
According to Virgil, this king of Troy was killed by Neoptolemus during the fall of Troy. His children included Paris and Deiphobus.

This daughter of Priam was given the gift of prophecy by Apollo, but her prophecies were cursed to never be believed by anyone. Following the war, she was taken captive by Agamemnon, resulting in her death at the hands of Clytemnestra and Aegisthus.

bonuses.leadin: Neoptolemus threw the infant Astyanax off the walls of this city. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Odin sacrificed this body part to Mimir in exchange for a drink from the Well of Urd. Odysseus injures one of these body parts belonging to Polyphemus ("pahl-lee-FEE-mus").
While attempting to steal the Mead of Poetry from Suttungr ("SOOT-ung-er"), Odin threw one of these things into the air, causing 9 slaves to all kill each other while attempting to retrieve it.
Odin kept two of these animals, called Huginn (thought) and Muninn (mind), as pets. Their job was to travel around the nine realms and report what they saw back to Odin.

bonuses.leadin: Answer a few questions about Odin, for 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this task that, in the folklore motif of the "Hand of Glory," can be performed by anyone carrying the dried hand of a hanged man. In addition to performing this task, the Hand of Glory was said to emit light only for its user and paralyze passersby.

The Hand of Glory recipe in the Petit Albert grimoire uses the "Lapland" type of this plant. Coincidentally, the name of this plant is used to open the thieves' cave in Antoine Galland's popular version of the Ali Baba story.
This villain from Slavic myth used a magically-locked chest containing a needle inside of a duck inside of a rabbit to hide his soul.

bonuses.leadin: In Slavic folklore, treasure hunters are said to trick hedgehogs and tortoises into revealing the location of the magical raskovnik herb by making them use it to perform this task. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this ship that contains wood from the grove of Dodona, allowing it to speak prophecies. This ship lends its name to the heroes who retrieved the Golden Fleece.
This ship is destined to depart to Vígríðr during Ragnarok after Jörmungandr's rage sets it free. It is made up of the untrimmed nails of the dead and captained by the jötunn Hrym.
This chief Egyptian god rides the solar barge Mesektet every night through the Duat, fighting the giant serpent Apep. He is most commonly associated with the sun.

bonuses.leadin: Boats play an important role in many myth systems. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this god spawned by Atum alongside his sister Tefnut.
Mekhit is often associated with this goddess, who was beheaded by the falcon Nemty and was known as the Mistress of Dendera. She wore the menat necklace and was sometimes known as Mehturt.

Hathor serves as the wrathful "Eye of Ra" in this New Kingdom text, which is often accompanied by a depiction of the solar barque on the back of the title animal, who is supported by Shu and various other gods.
acceptableAnswers: the Book of the Cow of Heaven

bonuses.leadin: He is often equated with the "lord of the lance" Onuris, who had to retrieve his lion consort Mekhit. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these mischievous figures from Native American folklore, who can vary from helpful to downright annoying. Raven and Crow are examples of these figures.
This trickster was responsible for creating people from a ball of mud. Sometimes known as "Old Man," this animal showed his more heroic side by defeating the Thunderbird in one story.
In another story, the Thunderbird drops one of these animals from the sky to the earth. In an Inuit tale, Raven discovers a lost girl by finding one of these animals.

bonuses.leadin: The spider god Iktomi is an example of this kind of figure. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This group venerates deities such as Chernobog, Baba-Yaga, and Svarog. Most of their myths come from folk tales and Pagan gods, both standing alone and being reconciled with the Christian religion as it came to Europe.

This figure is the head of the Slavic pantheon. He is often depicted as an eagle sitting atop the tallest branch of the sacred tree, where he watches over the entire world. He also killed Veles, the god of the underworld.
Perun is the god of this phenomenon, which is also his main weapon. Other famous deities such as Thor and Zeus are also gods of this.

bonuses.leadin: Answer some questions about a lesser-known European myth system. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this man whose journeys through the afterlife and witnesses dead souls drinking from the River Lethe.
The myth of Er appears in the tenth book of this Socratic Dialogue by Plato. This dialogue contains the Allegory of the Cave and the legend of the Ring of Gyges.

Because he did not drink from the Lethe, Er was able to recall seeing the Spindle of Necessity attended to by the goddess Ananke and these daughters of hers, who are described as daughters of Nyx in most other myths.

bonuses.leadin: This Son of Armenios of Pamphylia died in battle before being revived on his funeral pyre ten days later. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this Germanic god often depicted on skis carrying a bow.
Ydalir was considered a part of Alfheim, which was ruled by this Vanir god. His possessions include the golden boar Gullinbursti and the foldable ship Skidbladnir.
Because he had earlier relinquished his sword in an effort to woo Gerd, Frey was easily killed by the jotun Surt wrath during this final apocalyptic battle of Norse mythology.

bonuses.leadin: This god's home is called Ydalir and he is considered the daughter of Sif and the stepson of Thor. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this beast sent by a furious Ishtar to attack Gilgamesh after he spurns her romantic advances. Like Humbaba, this beast is slain by Gilgamesh and Enkidu, though Enkidu becomes ill and dies as punishment for killing it.

The Canaanite goddess Astarte ("uh-STAR-tee") was an even more warlike equivalent of Ishtar, likely because she absorbed aspects of this extremely metal goddess who loved to wade through the blood of her enemies. After the death god Mot kills Ba'al, this goddess kills him in revenge.

Worship of Ishtar and Astarte influenced the worship of this Greek goddess of beauty and love. Ishtar's journey to the underworld to save Tammuz can be seen as a parallel story to this goddess's love for Adonis.

bonuses.leadin: Ishtar threatens to release the dead and allow them to eat the living if she isn't allowed to send this beast to Earth. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Heracles strangled two of what type of creatures sent by Hera to kill him in his crib?
The Rainbow Serpent is a primordial deity of the people of this modern country.
This serpent, sometimes considered to be a dragon, gnaws on the roots of Yggdrasil, the World Tree of Norse myth.

bonuses.leadin: Echidna of Greek myth fame was half-woman, half one of these creatures. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this position held by Kay Kavus, who was captured by the White Div. His rescue was the sixth of seven labors undertaken by a legendary hero.
The Shahnameh, or Book of Kings, is an ancient Iranian epic by Firdowsi written in this language.
Kaveh the Blacksmith helped Fereydun overthrow this tyrant Shah, who had himself overthrown Jamshid. Ahriman cursed this man with two brain-eating snakes attached to his shoulders.

bonuses.leadin: Original language term required. One holder of this position owned a flying throne propelled by eagles. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this Hindu god of thunder and war who drinks soma and leads the Aryan conquest of India.
Indra appears in 250 hymns as the highest god in this ancient text. This text is the oldest of the four Sanskrit texts composed around the 2nd to 1st millenium BC.
Indra is often depicted riding Airavata, this type of creature. A god with the head of this creature is often depicted riding a mouse.

bonuses.leadin: After Hanuman mistook the Sun for a fruit and tried to swallow it, this god struck him with his thunderbolt. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this chief Olympian deity, who freed the Hecatonchires to help him fight against the Titans.
In his early life, Zeus was fed by Amalthea, a female animal of this kind. A god with the hindquarters, legs, and horns of this animal was the son of Hermes and Dryope.
During Zeus' infancy, Rhea enlisted the help of this group of dancers to make noise from their armor and weapons in order to drown out Zeus' cries.

bonuses.leadin: This god punished the Telchines for their malevolent use of magic, and also punished Salmoneus for mimicking him. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Odin had two of these birds, Huginn [HOO-gan] and Muninn [MOO-nin], named for thought and memory. They flew all over the world and reported what they had seen to Odin.
Ymir [EE-meer] created two of these creatures from his armpits. One of these creatures, named Angrboda ["anger"-boh-dah], is the consort of Loki, who is himself half-Aesir [AY-seer] and half-this.
Andvari [OND-vah-ree] was one of these creatures, who lived under a waterfall and had a gold ring. Other examples of these creatures forged Odin's spear and Thor's hammer.

bonuses.leadin: Identify the following creatures from Norse myth, for ten points each.

parts.text: Name this holiday on which Frau Perchta visits homes in the Alpine countryside with her retinue of unbaptized children, punishing the wicked by cutting open their bellies. In other traditions, bad children are punished on this holiday by Black Peter and the Krampus.

Perchta, like her northern counterpart Holda, was a patron of this craft and was often encountered with a golden tool used for it. The Norse goddess Frigg was famed for her skill in this craft, through which she made the clouds.
acceptableAnswers: any answer indicating textile creation such as knitting

parts.text: This mountain spirit from Silesian folklore is said to live in the Riesengebirge. He got his name after abducting a local princess and giving her a magic wand that let her turn turnips into companions.

bonuses.leadin: A folk figure associated with this holiday wanders the mountains blessing the shepherds' flocks and once blinded a servant for a year for spying on his master's family by hiding in a stove. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this creature of which a "surgeon's photograph" was taken in 1934 that has since been mostly debunked as a hoax. This large and long-necked creature supposedly inhabits a body of water in the Scottish Highlands.

Like the Loch (lock) Ness Monster, this creature is a cryptid, since its existence is unsubstantiated. This creature is described as a hairy and ape-like humanoid creature in North American forests which leaves giant footprints.

Sightings of this cryptid whose name means "goat-sucker" have mostly been in northern Mexico. This spiny creature supposedly the size of a large dog is said to attack and suck the blood from livestock.

bonuses.leadin: According to a text from the sixth century, this creature was stopped from attacking a monk's follower when Saint Columba made the sign of the cross and told it to back off. For 10 points each:

parts.text: The most famous drakaina was probably Typhon's consort Echidna, who was slain by this being. While guarding Io, this being was bored to death by the story of Pan and Syrinx.
Kronos tasked the drakaina Campe with guarding these one-eyed beings, who forged the gods' weaponry after Zeus killed Campe and freed them.
Apollo's epithet Delphinios may come from slaying the drakaina Delphyne, whom Typhon had earlier appointed to guard these things.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about Greek mythology's tradition of drakainai (drah-KAY-nye), or specifically female dragons or serpent monsters, for 10 points each.

parts.text: After the death of Solomon, this son of his inherited the throne. His tax levies angered the populace.
Rehoboam was the son of this Ammonite woman, the only wife of Solomon to be mentioned by name in the bible. Her name means "pleasant."
During the reign of Rehoboam, Judah was sacked by this Egyptian Pharaoh. This event is depicted on a relief at the Bubastis Portal at Karnak.

bonuses.leadin: Answer these questions about the dissolution of the united Jewish monarchy, for 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this activity. Interpretations of zombies in Haitian voodoo differ from "Romero zombies" whose performance of this cannibalistic activity was popularized by the film Night of the Living Dead.
acceptableAnswers: prompt on eating people with “What body part?”

parts.text: This ethnic group's water goddesses Ogbuide and Uhammiri are synonymous with Mami Wata deities. People of this ethnicity worship deities called arusi and are protected by guardians called chi against vengeful ogbanje.

The river orisha Oshun turned herself into a peacock and then a vulture to carry messages for this creator god of the Yoruba pantheon who is depicted as omnipotent in the heavens over humanity and orishas.

bonuses.leadin: In Zulu myth, the Mamlambo is a "goddess of rivers" who appears like an aquatic horse and performs this action on families who don't sacrifice regularly. For 10 points each:

parts.text: After he struck a pair of snakes, Hera turned Tiresias into one of these people. Tiresias displeased Hera again when he settled an argument between her and Zeus by admitting that these people enjoyed sex more than men.

Depending on the myth, either Zeus gave this gift to Tiresias as a reward for supporting his argument against Hera, or Athena gave Tiresias this ability. The god Apollo governed this skill, which he also gave to Cassandra.
Later in his life, Tiresias told this man to allow Antigone [an-tih-goh-nee] to bury her brother rather than imprison her for it. Though he refuses at first, this king of Thebes eventually agrees.

bonuses.leadin: Tiresias is a very busy character in Greek mythology. For 10 points each, answer some questions about his experiences.

parts.text: Name this sister of Joukahainen (YO-cuh-HIGH-nin) courted by the hero Vainamoinen (VAY-nuh-MOY-nin). Rather than marry him, she drowns herself, later becoming a mermaid whom Vainamoinen catches while fishing.

Vainamoinen has difficulty getting this type of tree to grow until five women and a giant burn grass to enrich the soil; he then cuts it down because it blocks the sun. Later, he is healed by a balm made from this type of tree.
The adventures of Vainamoinen are recorded in the Kalevala, an epic from this nation compiled by Elias Lonnrot whose other sections feature Lemminkainen (lem-in-KAI-nin) and Kullervo (koo-LEHR-voh).

bonuses.leadin: When this woman tells her mother she does not want to get married, her mother advises her to spend a year eating only butter, a year eating only bacon, and a year eating only desserts. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This goddess has a lion's head and a woman's body. Ra created her to destroy mankind, but when she got out of hand, he tricked her into drinking seven thousand jars of beer, transforming her into her counterpart Hathor.

Sekhmet is the wife and sister of this green-skinned god, the patron of craftsmen. He is depicted in the linens of a mummy and carries a was sceptre with a djed and an ankh. In some myths, he thought the universe into existence.

This city was the center of the Ptah cult. Ptah is part of this city's namesake triad, along with Sekhmet and Nefertem. It was the capital of the Old Kingdom, and was also notable for its huge statues of Ramses II.

bonuses.leadin: She bears on her head a solar disk and uraeus, a cobra. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this golden boar, whose name appropriately means "golden-bristled."
Gullinbursti worked for this sun, rain, and harvest god, whose other possessions included the collapsible boat Skidbladnir and a sword that killed giants of its own accord.
Brokk and Eitri were part of a group of skilled dwarves known as the "sons of" this figure.

bonuses.leadin: One of many cool things made by Brokk and Eitri, this creature's function is to pull a chariot. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this brother of Zeus and Greek god of the underworld.
Hades abducted this daughter of Demeter to be his wife. To make sure she would always have to return to the underworld, he tricked her into eating pomegranate seeds.
This man's music was so beautiful that Hades agreed to let him take his wife Eurydice back from the underworld, so long as neither looked back until they had left, which of course he did.

bonuses.leadin: He loaned his helmet of invisibility to Perseus. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this woman from Greek mythology, who was tormented by Hera and watched over by Argus Panoptes because of this woman's relationship with Zeus.

After this woman had an affair with Zeus, Hera took the completely reasonable response of turning her into a snake and then cursing her to never be able to close her eyes right before slaughtering all of this woman's children.
Because this nymph kept distracting Hera while Zeus was up to no good, Hera laid a curse on this nymph that prevented her from communicating with the object of her love, Narcissus.

bonuses.leadin: The Bosphorus strait was named for this woman after she crossed it while being chased by a stinging gadfly. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this religion in which a figure vowed to kill 1,000 people per day while another vowed to beget 1,500 people per day. One of this religion's key rituals involves drinking three cups of sake [sah-kay].
Followers of Shintoism worshiped these mythical figures, which include Izanagi, Izanami, and Amaterasu [ah-mah-teh-rah-soo].
Shintoism is an indigenous religion of this Asian country. Many Shinto torii gates can be found across this country at the entrance to Shinto shrines.

bonuses.leadin: The sun deity of this religion was lured out of a cave with a mirror. For ten points each:

parts.text: The Chimera had the head of a lion, as well as a tail that some sources say had a snake's head at its end. Its third head was one of this animal, coming from the middle of its back.
The nine-headed bird was an early form of the phoenix in this nation's mythology. This country's mythology also includes characters like Pangu and Sun Wukong.
This white elephant belonging to Indra had three heads and was the king of all elephants. It is able to suck up the waters of the underworld and spray them into the clouds.

bonuses.leadin: The more heads, the better! For 10 points each, name these things about mythological creatures with more than one head.

parts.text: Identify this queen of Lydia, possibly best-known for wearing the lionskin cloak of a certain hero during that hero's year of servitude under her.

This hero's accidental murder of Iphitus led to the aforementioned punishment, during which he fathered a son named Agelaus or Lamos with Omphale. His other adventures included the twelve labors he performed for Eurystheus.
During Heracles's time in Lydia, these rascally forest demons stole his weapons. In retribution, he tied them to a pole, heads downward. In another story, Zeus transformed them all into monkeys.

bonuses.leadin: This daughter of the river god Iardanus was married to the mountain god Tmolus, and when Tmolus was gored to death by a bull she ruled his kingdom on her own. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this trickster figure in many Native American myth systems.

In one tale, Coyote attempts to bring home his dead wife from the land of these creatures, who live in deep woods. In some myths, Coyote made these people on accident in a half-assed attempt to make humans.

The story of Coyote and the Shadow People is a myth of this Sahaptian-speaking tribe of the Columbia River Plateau. In a story share between the Ute and these probable Old Cordilleran descendants, Coyote attempts to cheat a porcupine out of some buffalo meat.

bonuses.leadin: In some myth systems, this creature created man from a mud ball and created the Milky Way by blowing on a bag of stars. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this Egyptian goddess who traveled to Byblos to recover a box for her husband Osiris, who was subsequently torn apart into fourteen pieces by his brother Set.

After creating a magic phallus for Osiris, Isis conceived Horus, who later married this goddess of love. This goddess transformed into Sekhmet and ravaged Egypt until the Nile was filled with wine to make her drunk.
This figure was the sister of Isis, Osiris, and Set. Some accounts of the birth of Anubis states that she was spurned by her husband Set and took on Isis' form before conceiving Anubis with Osiris.

bonuses.leadin: In one story she had a snake poison the sun god Ra and refused to heal him until he revealed his secret name, allowing her to gain power over him. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these items grown in the Garden of Hesperides, one of which disrupted the wedding of Peleus and Thetis and led to a beauty contest judged by Paris.
That beauty contest became the cause of this conflict after Paris received Helen of Sparta from Aphrodite. This conflict ended thanks to a namesake wooden "horse."
This goddess of discord threw the Apple of Discord because she was not invited to the wedding of Peleus and Thetis.

bonuses.leadin: Melanion gained the hand of Atalanta by dropping these objects during a race. For 10 points each-

parts.text: Name this Norse thunder god.
At the palace of Utgard-Loki, Thor could not pick up one of these animals, which was actually the Midgard Serpent. Freya's chariot is pulled by these animals.
Thor receives a cauldron for Aegir's feast by throwing a goblet at this giant, with whom he goes fishing for the Midgard Serpent.

bonuses.leadin: This deity killed Thrym after disguising himself as Freya to retrieve Mjollnir. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Give this Greek term for beings that sprung, often fully formed, from the soil.
Many autochthons (aw-TAHK-thuns) are described as children of this Titaness of the earth, who is the mother and wife of Uranus.

According to the Critias, all the kings of this land descended from an autochthonous being named Evenor. The primary source describing this mythical kingdom situates it beyond the pillars of Hercules.

bonuses.leadin: Thucydides says that two kings of Athens, Erechtheus (eh-REK-thee-us) and Cecrops ("KEY-crops"), wore jewelry made from cicadas in their hair since both cicadas and the kings had this unusual manner of birth. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this ancestral god of the Suwa clan, who fights the similarly-named Takemikazuchi ("TAH-keh-MEE-kah-ZOO-chee") in the first sumo wrestling match.
Takeminakata is most commonly the grandson of this Japanese storm god and brother of Amaterasu.

Takeminakata succeeds his father Okuninushi ("OH-KOO-nee-NOO-shee") as the ruler of this historical region of Japan. This is where Okuninushi helps the hare of Inaba, and where Susanoo slays Yamato-no-Orochi.

bonuses.leadin: Upon his arrival, this deity feuds with the native god Moreya for sovereignty over Nagano and central Japan. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this legendary war, in which Agamemnon, Odysseus, and the combined forces of Greece besieged an enemy city-state.
Agamemnon returns from the Trojan War with Cassandra, a Trojan princess who had been given this gift by Apollo, though she had also been cursed so that no one believed her predictions.
The Oresteia is by this Greek playwright, who also wrote Prometheus Bound and Seven Against Thebes.

bonuses.leadin: In the Oresteia [oh-ress-TYE-ah] trilogy, Agamemnon returns from this war only to be murdered by his wife, Clytemnestra. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name this beautiful mortal man and lover of Aphrodite. Aphrodite asks him not to go out to hunt, but he does anyway and is killed by a wild boar.
Adonis was born out of a tree that used to be this woman. This woman was transformed into a tree as punishment for having sex with her father, King Cinyras ("sin-NYE-russ").

In the Metamorphoses, the story of Adonis is framed as a song sung by this musician. This hero travels to the underworld to bring back his wife Eurydice ("yoo-RID-uh-see"), but he fails since he turns back to look at her.

bonuses.leadin: This character's name derives from a Canaanite word for "Lord," which has the same root as a Hebrew word that may substitute for the name Yahweh ("YAH-way") when speaking aloud. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these half-bird, half-woman creatures from Greek mythology. These creatures, when not serving as the "hounds of Zeus," regularly carried off evildoers to the Erinyes.

The harpies would have continued harassing Phineus, likely to the end of time, if it wasn't for the intervention of this leader of the Argonauts. Phineus thanked this man by telling him how to get past the Symplegades, which allowed this man to continue his quest for the Golden Fleece.
In some stories, Jason also needed the help of Calais and Zetes, the sons of a god of this specific phenomenon. Boreas, the bringer of winter, was a god of this specific phenomenon.

bonuses.leadin: These creatures were tasked by Zeus to destroy Phineus's food to punish him for revealing a prophecy given by Zeus. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name this bad-tempered lightning god for whom the Sons of Ivaldi created the hammer Mjolnir [mee-YOLL-neer]. During Ragnar¨ok, the Norse apocalypse, this god and the great serpent Jormungandr [YOR-mun-gon-dur] will kill each other in battle.
This queen of the Vanir, the Norse nature gods, owned a magical cloak made of falcon feathers which she could use to fly. She claimed half the souls of dead warriors for her mead-hall, F´olkvangr.
This Norse goddess used her mystical spinning wheel to create the clouds. This wife of Odin is the goddess of both family life and clairvoyance.

parts.text: Name this demigod who cleaned the Augean Stables on the instructions of Eurystheus.
Heracles fought the river god Achelous for the hand of this third wife, who inadvertently killed him with a shirt soaked in the poisonous blood of Nessus.
One story relates that this god loaned Heracles a golden goblet which he used to sail across the sea. This god turned Arge into a doe for claiming she could hunt a stag that ran as fast as him.

bonuses.leadin: This character captured the Ceryneian Hind and stole the Girdle of Hippolyta. For 10 points each:

parts.text: While trying to escape from Crete with artificial wings, this boy ignored warnings to not fly too close to the sun. As a result, the wax holding the feathers together melted, causing him to fall and drown in the sea.
This master craftsman, Icarus's father, was locked away in Crete with Icarus after King Minos ordered him to build the Labyrinth.
The Labyrinth was made to house this creature that had the head of a bull and body of a man. This creature was eventually killed by Theseus.

bonuses.leadin: Hubris is one of the leading causes of death in Greek myth. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name this snake-haired Gorgon from Greek myth, whose gaze turned those who looked at her to stone.
This Greek hero slew Medusa with the help of a reflective shield, which allowed him to see her withoutbeing frozen by her gaze.
Perseus cut off Medusa's head and gave it to Athena, who had set it into the center of this object, her shield.

bonuses.leadin: This mythical figure was the mortal sister of Stheno and Euryale[yoo-REE-ah-lee], and she wascursedinto her most famous form by Athena. For ten points each,

parts.text: Identify this object which was eventually stolen by Cet, and used to fulfill the prophecy that the king of Leinster would have his revenge after death.

The brain ball of Mesgegra was used to kill this high king of Ulster, and noted pursuer of Deirdre, when it was used as a shot in a sling. The ball lodged there until, as later Christian legend has it, this king heard about the death of Christ and got so angry that his wound burst and he died.

The conflict over Deirdre and the murder of Noisiu by Conchobar drove this man, Conchobar's stepfather, into an allegiance with Medb. He died when Lugaidh, a warrior in the service of Ailil, Medb's husband, killed him after Ailil became jealous.

bonuses.leadin: This object was possessed by Conall, who obtained it after killing the king of Leinster and cutting off his head, which he then found impossible to lift. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Jason was the captain of this ship, which set sail to capture the Golden Fleece. This ship, which had a prophetic mast from the grove of Dodona, housed such sailors as Orpheus, Castor and Pollux, and for a limited time Heracles.
The argonauts set sail toward this city, where a dragon protects the golden fleece. Medea is a princess from this land.

During their escape from Colchis, the argonauts needed a distraction to escape the Colchan navy. Medea planned for this, and chopped this person, her younger brother, into pieces and scattered them on the sea, forcing the enemy ships to pick them up for proper burial.

bonuses.leadin: During the hunt for the Calydonian boar, Jason killed some hunting dogs with his spear. Somehow, Jason still became the leader of his own quest. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this man from Greek mythology who journeyed to the Underworld to retrieve his dead wife Eurydice, but failed the trial after he turned to look back at her.
Orpheus used music to drown out these birdlike women's alluring song for the Argonauts. Odysseus tied himself to a mast so he could hear them without getting eaten.
Using music from his lyre, Orpheus brought this daughter of Demeter and wife of Hades to tears. Her time in the Underworld for half the year causes winter.

bonuses.leadin: He was torn apart by Maenads for playing miserable music after his most famous venture. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this hero from the Ulster Cycle, who wielded the spear Gae Bolg and got a new name after killing a fierce dog.
Cu Chulainn fought off the armies of Queen Medb at this mythical battle over a prized bull, though he was forced to slay his foster brother Ferdiad during it.
Cu Chulainn and Ferdiad both studied under this warrior woman, who taught Cu Chulainn to use the deadly Gae Bolg.

bonuses.leadin: This character is the son of Deichtine and the sun god Lugh. For 10 points each:

Like kitsune, these jolly creatures also shapeshift, but often with the help of leaves. In the tale "Bunbuku Chagama," one of these animals transforms himself into a teapot with legs and walks a tightrope to earn money for his rescuer.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, name some animals with magical powers in Japanese folklore.

parts.text: Name this Indian epic about the title man's attempt to rescue his wife, Sita, from the Demon King, Ravana, with the help of an army of monkeys.
The army of monkeys that helps Rama is led by this Hindu monkey-god, who was blessed by Shiva with strength and immortality.
During Rama's journey, Bharata places these articles of clothing belonging to Rama on the throne to indicate that Bharata is only serving as a regent.

parts.text: Athena gave the golden apples of Hesperides to this Greek goddess, who later gifted the apples to Hippomenes so he could use them to win the hand of Atalanta.

When this goddess, the provider of the apples that helped maintain the youth and immortality of the Norse gods, was kidnapped by a giant, Loki transformed her into a nut in order to carry her back to Asgard easily.
After this legendary man was mortally wounded in the Battle of Camlann by his son, he went to Avalon, which translates into "isle of apple trees," to recover.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, name these things about apples in mythology.

parts.text: Name this goddess of fire who resides in Kilauea and created several islands via volcanic eruptions.

Pele is a goddess from the mythology of these people, whose other deities include I'o (ee-oh), the source of all who breathed life into Kane, the creator god. Temples from this mythology are called heiau (hay-ow).

Another creation story of the Hawai'ian Islands involves this trickster deity, who pulled them up from the ocean on his fishing line. In Maori mythology, this figure lengthens the day by restraining the sun with a jawbone.

bonuses.leadin: This deity was banished from Tahiti for fighting with her sister Na-mako-o-Kaha'i, the Goddess of the Sea. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this wife of Menelaus, whose kidnapping by Paris sparked the Trojan War.

In the play Helen, the title character is actually taken by the gods to this kingdom, where she narrowly escapes marriage to Theoclymenus. In real life, the syncretic god Serapis was worshiped here after its conquest by Alexander.
In a myth often depicted in art, Menelaus threatened to kill Helen during the sack of Troy, but spared her after she killed her husband and performed this other action.

In the Benne Alankara ritual, Hindus smear statues of Ganesha with this food item, which is called ghee in its clarified form.

According to Apollonius Rhodius, when Typhon had his arms stretched out wide, 100 of these objects were visible, which allowed him to burn things.

parts.text: Name this event from Norse mythology. For no apparent reason, Thor kills the dwarf Litr at this event by kicking him into a fire.

parts.text: Give the common two-word English term for this creature that lives in waterholes and, in many stories, creates the world during a prehistoric era called the Dreamtime.
Various versions of the Rainbow Serpent appear in the myths of the indigenous peoples of Australia, who are collectively referred to with this term.

In an Aboriginal story about the origin of death, one of these animals debates with a crab about the best way to die. A three-legged example of these animals called yata-garasu led the first Japanese emperor, Jimmu, to his new homeland.

bonuses.leadin: The Gunwinggu ("gun-WING-goo") people call this creature Ngalyod ("NYAH-lod") and believe it rests under billabongs ("BILL-uh-bongs") during the dry season. For 10 points each:

parts.text: The daughters of Nyx or Atlas, these three Greek goddesses are the goddesses of the evening and sunset.
This sun God became angry after Odysseus's men ate some of his sacred cattle. He is known for appearing each day in a horse-drawn chariot.
This Titan goddess of the dawn is the sister of Helios and lover of Tithinus, who was turned into a grasshopper after this goddess forgot to ask Zeus to grant him eternal youth.

bonuses.leadin: Identify these gods and goddesses from Greek myth with something in common for 10 points each,

parts.text: Name these four objects personified by the four sons of Horus, each of one was meant for a different organ.
Duamutef, the personification of the canopic jar for the stomach, was protected by this goddess of hunting and weaving. In some traditions, she was considered the mother of Sobek.
Duamutef had the head of this animal, as did the underworld deity Anubis.

bonuses.leadin: These objects were personified by the four deities Imsety, Duamutef, Hapi, and Qebehsenuef, who each also had a companion goddess to protect them. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this Ancient Greek dramatist, who also described the city of Cloudcuckooland in The Birds.

This first prize-winning Aristophanes work sees Dionysus travel to Hades to recover Euripides [yew-RIH-pih-deez], the "greatest Athenian tragedian." The title characters of this play are a chorus that chants "Brekekekex-koax-koax."

After a debate, this author of The Persians, Seven Against Thebes, and the Oresteia [ohr-eh-STY-uh] trilogy is brought back instead of Euripides. Adding insult to injury, this man suggests that Sophocles take his place as Hades' best tragic poet while he's away.

bonuses.leadin: Lampito and Myrrhine ["mere"-een] agree to Lysistrata's [liss-iss-trah-tah ‟s] scheme to end the Peloponnesian War in one of this man's plays. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name these events hosted by a sea god at Hlesey (L'YES-ay"). Another one of these events is the setting of the Lokasenna("LOH-kah-sen-uh"), in which Loki insults the attendants and kills the servant Fimafeng ("FEE-mah-feng").
acceptableAnswers: answers that describe a meal hosted by Aegir

parts.text: In the Skáldskaparmál("SKAL-skap-ur-mall"), Aegir is told about how the gods started to age when the kidnapping of Idunn ("EE-thohn") deprived them of these fruits. Hippomenes ("hih-PAH-muh-neez") threw these fruits on the ground to distract Atalanta in a footrace.
The Skáldskaparmál also tells the story of these two giantesses with rhyming names, who ran a mill to create gold for King Fróði ("FROH-thee"), and later salt for the sea-king Mysing. Name either.

bonuses.leadin: The Hymiskviða("HOO-may-SKVEE-thuh") follows the Aesir's ("acer's") quest to find a kettle large enough to be used at one of these events, which they eventually obtain from Hymir ("HOO-mair"). For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these animals, which include the Akan trickster figure Anansi.

In a story possibly inspired by Anansi, this African American trickster figure gets stuck to a doll made of tar after attacking it. This character is often antagonized by a similarly named fox and bear.
In this Congolese hero's namesake epic, Master Spider saves him from falling into spike pits during a dancing contest. This hero defeats his father with the help of his conga-scepter, a flyswatter.

bonuses.leadin: One of these animals captures four dangerous creatures to obtain the stories of the world from Nyame. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This god was suckled by the goat Amalthea and suspended from a tree by the nymph Adamanthea during his time on Mount Ida. His mother Rhea had given birth to him in a cave on Crete in order to hide him from his father Cronus.
This group of figures, who are often conflated with the Phrygian Korybantes and the Lemnian Cabeiri, danced and banged their spears on their shields during Zeus's birth to drown out his cries.
This decad of demigods was born when Rhea dug her hands into the earth during labor. Three Phrygian ones named Acmon, Damnameneus, and Celmis are said to have invented the art of iron-forging.

bonuses.leadin: Identify some inhabitants of Mount Ida, for 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this sun god, who defeated Apep every day while sailing the "sun boat" across the sky.

This god was syncretized with Ra as Ra-Horakhty. This son of Isis and Osiris had eyes representing the sun and moon, and defeated Set in a boat race by using a boat made of wood painted to look like stone.
Like Horus, Khepri, and Atum, this patron of Thebes was also syncretized with Ra after the rule of Ahmose I. When this wind god was combined with Ra, he was depicted as a red-eyed, lion-headed man.

bonuses.leadin: Ancient Egyptians called themselves the "cattle of" this leader of the Egyptian pantheon, who was often depicted with a falcon head. For 10 points each,

parts.text: What four-legged creatures with snake-like bodies are ubiquitous and important in Chinese myth and are very different from fire-breathing European versions?
Yinglong is a deity associated with this phenomenon. Tlaloc was an Aztec deity of this phenomenon who was propitiated to help with agriculture by baby sacrifice.
Dragons and tigers adorn the roofs of temples in this Chinese philosophical tradition that also venerates the Eight Immortals.

bonuses.leadin: Yinglong, a Chinese deity, takes this form. For 10 points each:

This son of Iapetus and Themis stole fire from the gods to give to humans and, afterwards, had his liver repeatedly eaten.
This Welsh god of agriculture, the son of Don, stole a hound, a deer, and a bird from Arawn and thus kicked off the Battle of the Trees, in which his brother Gwydion turned the trees into fighters.

bonuses.leadin: Name some assorted figures from myth who caused trouble, For 10 points each.

parts.text: Name this creator deity, who sent about four hundred lesser spirits to Earth to act as intermediaries. Obatala creates human bodies, but they are not alive until this god breathes "emi" into them.
E. Bolaji Idowu's book Olodumare is subtitled for God in the belief of this West African ethnic group, whose worship of orishas spread through such diasporic religions as Santeria and Candomble.
The Aja, Ewe, and Fon practice a traditional religion of this name. Yoruba-influenced syncretic Cuban, Dominican, Louisianan, and Haitan religions of this name venerate loa.

bonuses.leadin: Oshun transforms into a peacock to fly to this deity and ask him to end a drought, but as her feathers fall off and are scorched by the sun, she becomes a vulture. For 10 points each:

parts.text: The Cretan Bull ended up mating with Pasiphae, the wife of this king of Crete who later became a judge in the underworld.
From that union came this monster, which resided in a labyrinth designed by Daedalus and was slain by Theseus with the help of Ariadne.
The Cretan Bull was supposed to be sacrificed to this god, but when Minos wanted to keep it, this god caused Pasiphae to fall in love with it.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer the following about the Cretan Bull.

parts.text: At Ragnarök, this son of Loki will break free of Gleipnir, a chain made of impossible materials, and kill Odin. Like Hati and Skoll, who devour the sun and moon, he is a wolf.
This son of Odin, who actually survives Ragnarök, avenges his father's death by ripping Fenrir apart.
Loki both kills and is killed by this god, a son of nine mothers who guarded the rainbow bridge Bifrost and sounded the Gjallarhorn. He is the last god to die at Ragnarök.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer some questions about the events of Ragnarök.

parts.text: Name this crafty Greek hero who helped design the Trojan horse.
According to Homer, Odysseus spent eight of those ten years held captive by this sea nymph, who had fallen in love with Odysseus.
Odysseus nearly made it home at the beginning of his trip, but a bag of wind from this god was opened prematurely and blew Odysseus's ship all the way back to Troy.

bonuses.leadin: He spent 10 years at sea, eventually floating home to Ithaca on driftwood. For 10 points each:

parts.text: The Peach Blossom Spring is a hidden paradise in this thought system's mythology. Poems in this myth system confer immortality on the Peach Blossom Spring and compare them with grotto-heavens.

Also known as the Isle of the Blessed, this place is located at the far western edge of the Earth adjacent to Oceanus. It is ruled by Rhadamanthus and is the destination of the particularly righteous in Greek mythology.

In Slavic myth, the elusive island of Buyan is home to the winds as well as this "deathless" villain. This decrepit old man stays alive by hiding his soul inside a needle, which is inside of a rabbit which is inside a buried chest.

bonuses.leadin: Name these paradises wherein everyone is immortal. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this hideous object with snakes for hair that could turn any living thing to stone. The blood that spurted from it gave rise to Pegasus and Chrysaor.
Unlike her sisters Stheno and Euryale, Medusa was the only one of these petrifying hideous creatures that was mortal. Blood from their right side revives, while blood from their left kills.
Medusa's head was ultimately mounted on this object of Athena's, where the head serves to terrify her enemies. It is made out of goat-skin.

bonuses.leadin: According to Ovid, beautiful coral was created when Perseus delicately placed this item onto soft leaves. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this son of Venus and Anchises who leads the Trojan survivors on a journey to Latium in his namesake Virgilian epic.

Upon his arrival in Latium, Aeneas began to court Latinus's daughter Lavinia; however, this angered Juno, who demanded that Lavinia be married to this king of the Rutulians. Aeneas kills him at the end of the Aeneid.

After encountering Aeneas at the Strophades, the harpy Celaeno angrily prophesies that the Trojans won't be able to build their city until they perform this ostensibly unpleasant action. Ascanius later realizes that they have accidentally accomplished it using bread.

bonuses.leadin: This man's prayers to Jupiter for safe passage to Italy are answered, but in exchange his helmsman Palinurus dies. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this man who was punished when he lusted after Hera at the feast. He was strapped to a fiery wheel in Hades.

Ixion actually was only lusting after a cloud named Nephele, though, and their relationship ended up spawning this race. This race of hybrid creatures fought the Lapiths at Pirithous' wedding, as depicted at the Parthenon.
Nephele is also known for being the mother of Phrixus and Helle, and sent them this object to take them to Colchis. Jason and the Argonauts quested after this object.

bonuses.leadin: This man killed his father-in-law Deioneus after refusing to pay a dowry, but after committing the first parricide in Greek myth, he was rewarded with a feast at Olympus. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this man, the subject of the Argonautica, who eloped with Medea after stealing the golden fleece from Colchis.

In the Argonautica, Medea does this action to her brother Absyrtus to slow the pursuit of her father Aeetes. Later, she convinced Pelias's daughters to do this to him after doing this to a ram and putting it in a cauldron.
The golden fleece was from a magic flying ram that carried this man's children Phrixus and Helle to Colchis. This man had been convinced to sacrifice those children by his evil wife Ino.

bonuses.leadin: This hero's expedition successfully passed through the Symplegades rocks after a dove was able to do so. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this brother of Regin, who was killed while in the form of an animal by one of the Aesir. His father, Hreidmar, demanded a ransom from the Aesir.
This trickster god was responsible for the murder of Otter, and he also acquired the ransom by holding up a dwarf named Andvari.
For his various misdeeds, Loki was eventually chained up below a poison-dripping snake, and this wife of Loki attends him and catches the poison in a bowl.

bonuses.leadin: His name now makes up part of a kenning for "gold." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this dual-wielding activity, whose pre-game rituals saw participants "go to the water" with a shaman before receiving 300 ritualistic cuts meant to secure victory. This activity, which the Cherokee called anetsa, was used to settle minor disputes in order to dissuade war.
The Iroquois legend of the Creator's Game more closely resembles this other sport derived from stickball. Ireland withdrew from this sport's 2022 World Games to allow the Haudenoasunee to compete.
In one tale, this culture hero introduces lacrosse to the Wabanaki after defeating the wizard Winpe. In another tale, this figure defeats a giant frog that consumed the world's water supply.

bonuses.leadin: In the Cherokee version of the "Creator's Game" tale, bat and flying squirrel receive their aerial attributes during this "great ballgame" between the animals and the birds. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Spock's father hails from this planet, which shares its name with the Roman god of fire.
Close relatives of the Vulcans come from this planet, named after a mythical twin of Remus raised by a she-wolf. The people of this planet are known for piloting warbirds.
In the episode "Who Mourns for Adonais?", the Enterprise approaches a planet named for this immortal son of Leda, before being grabbed by a giant green hand.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, name these planets from Star Trek that share their names with Greco-Roman figures.

parts.text: The end of the Trojan war was facilitated by the Trojan Horse, which was an idea given to this hero by Athena. Other notable actions of his include tricking a cyclops by introducing himself as "Nobody".

The strongest hero in the Trojan War was this near-invincible warrior whose only weak spot was a point on his heel. He attained this near invulnerability after being dipped in the River Styx by his mother.
The Trojan War began after the kidnapping of Helen by this hero. He is the person who slew Achilles by shooting him in the heel with an arrow, and was a son of King Priam, along with Hector.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer the following about heroes who fought in the Trojan War:

parts.text: Name this epic poem by Homer.

The Iliad begins with an invocation for the Muse to "sing of the rage of" this hero, who returns to battle in dramatic fashion after the death of his friend Patroclus. Homer does not include this man's death, which supposedly comes from an arrow to the heel.

Achilles fights and kills this prince of Troy, then drags his body around the city for twelve days. The epic ends with Achilles relenting and returning this man's body to his father, Priam, who then stages a funeral.

bonuses.leadin: This epic opens with a scene in which Agamemnon takes the maid Briseis from the protagonist, leading that protagonist to refuse to fight. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this daughter of Agamemnon who according to Calchas must be sacrificed to Artemis to guarantee wind for the departing Greek forces.
The sacrifice or near sacrifice took place in this Boeotian port from which the Greeks set sail for the Trojan War.

The story of Artemis rescuing Iphigenia is found in this now lost first member of the Epic Cycle. This eleven book prequel to the Iliad is summarized in depth by Proclus and is most often attributed to Stasinus.

bonuses.leadin: In one story, this figure helps her brother Orestes steal the statue of Artemis from the land of Tauris. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this crop, which formed the "Three Sisters" of Native American staple crops along with beans and squash.
The Green Corn Ceremony features a dance named for these objects. These objects, which are distributed by a Colorado-based "National Registry," provide an alternate name for the "fancy dance."
Feathers are also used in Southwestern dances for this purpose, the effects of which would lead to a bountiful harvest of crops.

bonuses.leadin: Many Native American nations, including the Seminole and Creek, held a harvest ceremony named for a "Green" one of these crops. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this food goddess from Shinto mythology, who apparently met her death after daring to offer food she spat up to another god, who promptly killed her.

Uke-Mochi's killer was this figure from Shinto mythology, who was created by Izanagi after the creation of Japan and climbed a ladder to his home in Takamagahara. After killing Uke-Mochi, his sister, Amaterasu, was very upset at him.

Tsukiyomi was the god of this object within Shinto mythology. The story goes that after Tsukiyomi murdered Uke-Mochi, Amaterasu vowed never to see him face to face, explaining a certain celestial division.

bonuses.leadin: After dying, this figure's eyebrows became silkworms and wheat and beans came from her genitals. For ten points each:

parts.text: Name the preserver god of Hinduism, who is known for his many avatars, which include Rama and the aforementioned Vamana.
One of the avatars of Vishnu was this charioteer of Arjuna. In that position he gives Arjuna advice on battle, which became the Bhagavad Gita.
This goddess was Vishnu's consort. She was the goddess of wealth and prosperity, and she is often pictured with two or four elephants.

bonuses.leadin: This god rides on the eagle Garuda, and in one form, he defeated the demon lord Bali. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this ancient Sanskrit epic that focuses on the title prince rescuing his wife Sita from Ravana.
Prince Rama is the seventh avatar of this Hindu preserver god. This god forms the Trimurti [tree-moor-tee] with Brahma and Shiva.

Rama is helped in his attempt to rescue Sita by Hanuman, one of these animals, who uses his tail to set fire to Ravana's palace. In illustrations of the Ramayana, Hanuman is often modeled after a Rhesus one of these animals.

One of the Olympians Diomedes wounded was this Greek god of war, who came onto the battlefield after Diomedes injured his lover, Aphrodite.

Diomedes managed to trade his bronze armor for the more valuable gold armor of this grandson of Bellerophon. After Diomedes revealed that his own grandfather had hosted Bellerophon, this man had his wits stolen by Zeus.

bonuses.leadin: This figure became the first human to wound two Olympians in a single day, when he was aided by the goddess Athena. For 10 points each:

This mother of Meleager and wife of Oeneus originally overheard the Fates at Meleager's birth and rescued the brand from the fire, but burned it to avenge Meleager's killing of her brother and nephew.
Meleager killed his relatives during the hunt for the Calydonian type of this animal, which was sent out by Artemis to avenge a snub in worship.

bonuses.leadin: This object was destroyed in retaliation for the killing of Toxeus and Plexippus, who insulted Atalanta. For 10 points each:

This German theorist analyzed the Buphonia ritual in his study of the role of sacrifice in ancient Greek religion, Homo Necans.
The Odyssey also features an elaborate description of the sacrifice of a heifer belonging to Nestor, who conducts that sacrifice in honor of this visiting son of Odysseus.

parts.text: This tetralogy by T.H. White begins with the novel The Sword And The Stone, and it's title references the prophecy that Arthur will become king again sometime in the future. It was found to actually have a 5th book, The Book of Merlyn.

This compilation of tales and translations by the violent criminal Sir Thomas Malory was written while he was imprisoned. It is divided into 21 books, and much of it's narrative structure is credited to the printer Thomas Caxton.

This Welsh compilation of tales was based on The White Book of Rhydderch and The Red Book of Hergest and one part deals with the conflict between Pryderi and math. It's Three Romances focus on Owain, Peredur, Geraint, and Enid, and is cited as a source for Chretien's Arthurian romances.

bonuses.leadin: Identify these works which deal with Arthurian myth For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this deity, who is often depicted with a serpent around his neck and a crescent moon on his forehead. This member of the Hindu trimurti often carries a weapon called the Trishula.
This wife of Shiva is sometimes represented as a yoni alongside a lingam. Her incarnations include Kali and Durga.

Before his implied intervention at Marathon, this deity had asked Pheidippides why the Athenians had failed to honor him despite his friendship. In gratitude, the Athenians built a sanctuary dubbed this god's "Cave" beneath the Acropolis.

Nestor's son Antilochus is killed by this Ethiopian king. This son of Eos and Tithonus is killed when Achilles stabs him with a spear.

This foolish king got the ears of a donkey after judging against Apollo in a music contest. He also wished that everything he touched would turn into gold, leaving him unable to eat.

The horse Sleipnir belongs to this chief Norse god, the husband of Frigg and father of Thor.

bonuses.leadin: This god was punished by being tied to a rock and having a snake drip poison onto his face. For 10 points each:

This father of Pelops served him to the Olympians. This man also stole ambrosia and nectar and was punished by being unable to reach some water and low-hanging fruit despite it being right there.
One granddaughter of Pelops was this wife of Amphitryon and later Rhadamanthys. She was aided by Lucina and Galanthis in giving birth to Hercules.

bonuses.leadin: This figure enlisted Myrtilus to aid him in a task that thirteen suitors died trying to do. For 10 points each:

This giant lumberjack in American folklore is accompanied by Babe the Blue Ox.

parts.text: Name this youngest son of Kronos, whose domain is the sky. This Greek God wields the thunderbolt.
Zeus was hidden in a cave on Mount Ida where he was raised by this she-goat. The Cornucopia is sometimes said to have originated from a broken horn belonging to this figure.
According to some sources, Zeus was hung from one of these objects to ensure that he was not in the sea, on land, or in the sky, and thus invisible to Kronos, who ruled over those three domains.

bonuses.leadin: According to Ovid, this god sent an eagle to retrieve the remains of the slain Ophiotaurus and burned them to ensure the Olympians' victory in the Titanomachy. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this herald of the Greek forces during the Trojan War. In the Iliad, Hera likens herself to this character as she speaks with the voice of "fifty men" to the Greeks, shaming them for fleeing the field of battle.
Unfortunately, Stentor's voice did not give him the super strength he needed to defeat this god in a shouting contest, so Stentor's lungs burst from exhaustion. This god carried the caduceus staff.

This god took a lot of credit for the gods' victory in the Titanomachy because his great shout frightened the Titans. He lends his name to a type of fear, which he caused by shouting loudly after being awoken from naps.

parts.text: Name this Greek goddess of love and beauty.
Aphrodite's jealous husband was this god, who in some stories fell from Olympus after Hera created him by herself.
Aphrodite was also the lover of this extraordinarily beautiful mortal man, and became so distraught at this man's death during a hunt that she caused anemone flowers to bloom where his blood fell.

bonuses.leadin: This goddess had an affair with Ares, which was revealed when her husband captured them together in a fine net and dragged them to Olympus in shame. For 10 points each,

bonuses.leadin: A spider was mocked by builders of this structure for attempting to contribute to its construction. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Alpheus pursued this nymph, who spurned his advances and eventually transformed into a fountain in Sicily. She is interrogated by Demeter since she saw who abducted her daughter.
