bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, name these nymphs.

parts.text: This "middle land," the realm of men, was formed by Ymir's [ee-meer's] eyebrow. It is encircled by a namesake "Serpent," and during Ragnarök, it will sink into the sea.
Midgard is connected to Asgard by this rainbow bridge, which is guarded by Heimdall.
This realm, separated from Asgard by the river Ifing, contains frost giants that pester both gods and men in Norse mythology.

bonuses.leadin: Identify the following important locations in Norse myth, for 10 points each,

parts.text: Name this husband of Nanna, the Norse god of light and happiness who was killed by an arrow made of mistletoe.
This trickster god was Odin's blood brother and engineered Balder's death along with fathering Hel, and the Midgard Serpent.
This mother of Baldr forced all the objects in the world not to harm her son, mistakenly thinking that mistletoe was too young to make such an agreement.

bonuses.leadin: Name some characters from Norse mythology, for 10 points each:

parts.text: These birds can cause storms merely by flapping their huge wings. Their archnemeses are whales.
Like Raven, this canine figure is most often portrayed as a trickster. In one story, he plays a hilarious trick called the Vomit Exchange on Owl.

These creatures appear in many variations of the Sedna myth. In one story, Sedna's father forces her to marry one of these birds, but she runs away, which then forces her father to cut her fingers off.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, name some creatures from Native American myth that don't show up much in other myth systems.

parts.text: Who is this Greek who was killed by a Trojan warrior while wearing the armor of his "friend," Achilles.
Patroclus was killed by this husband of Andromache, the greatest Trojan fighter.
Patroclus's dead body was guarded from desecration by Odysseus and this Greek warrior; later, after Achilles's death, this hero commits suicide when Odysseus is given his armor.

bonuses.leadin: This son of Monoetius killed Sarpedon outside the walls of Troy but was killed soon after. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this bard, who contests with Ilmarinen for the hand of Louhi's daughter, and in another episode enters into the stomach of the giant Antero Vipunen to find some magic words.
Vainamoinen is the hero of this poem by Elias Lonnrot, the national epic of Finland.
In the Kalevala, Kullervo owns one of these creatures named Musti. Cerberus is one of these with three heads.

bonuses.leadin: This figure enters into a singing contest with a rival who he sinks into the ground through his magic, agreeing to free him only when that rival offers his sister Aino in marriage. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Tlaloc and the aforementioned god reigned on the Templo Mayor in Tenochtitlan in this mythology, in an empire ruled by Montezuma.
Hernan Cortes was mistaken to be this Aztec feathered-serpent god. He is the virgin twin of Xolotl.
Tezcatlipoca, the god of the night sky, turned into one of these predators to get revenge on Quetzalcoatl in one myth. Aztec warriors sometimes dressed as these big cats.

bonuses.leadin: People made human sacrifices to Huitzilopochtli (hoo-EETZ-a-lo-PAHKT-lee). For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this event in which a figure was overthrown by his youngest son, leading to the Golden Age. Aphrodite is said to be born from the sea foam that resulted from this event.
acceptableAnswers: accept Kronos in place of Cronus
accept Uranus in place of Ouranos

parts.text: The overthrow of Ouranos was undergone at the urging of this mother of Cronus, who also created his sickle. This primordial deity is the mother of all Titans and is the personification of Earth.
Cronus is often said to use a sickle made from either flint or a hard stone material known by this word. This word survives today mainly as an adjective.

bonuses.leadin: After this event, the cyclops and hecatoncheires were re-imprisoned under the guard of the monstrous Campe. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This once-beautiful nymph was transformed into a six-headed monster that lived in a cave opposite a whirlpool, where she ate sailors.
Scylla was turned into a monster by this witch due to her rejection by the sea-god Glaucus. She also turned Odysseus' men into swine.
Most myths said the father of Scylla was this "old man of the sea" who became the father of a bunch of strange offspring with his monstrous sister Ceto.

bonuses.leadin: Answer some questions about a Greek myth, For 10 points each.

parts.text: Alviss was killed by this Norse god. He once lost a wrestling match to a personification of Old Age, and he will kill his archenemy, the World Serpent, at Ragnarok before walking nine paces and dying.

Thor was unhappy about his daughter Thrud being promised to Alviss, so he asked Alviss questions to test his wisdom until the sun came up, which did this to the dwarf. The gaze of Medusa also performed this action.
Being a dwarf, Alviss' homeworld would have been this dark world in Norse mythology.

bonuses.leadin: Alviss the dwarf was very abused during his lifetime. Answer some questions about him for 10 points each:

parts.text: This thunder god is often depicted with his companion Fujin. He is said to eat the navels of children and is depicted as a demon beating drums. One source states that hiding behind a mosquito net gives you immunity to his powers.
After Izanami died giving birth to this god of fire, eight gods of thunder sprang forth from her body. This deity was cut by his father into eight pieces which subsequently became eight volcanoes.
This kami is the god of the sea and lives in a similarly named palace. He owns two jewels that can control the tides and is waited on by half-human fish.

bonuses.leadin: Name some Shinto kami. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This Inca sun god was frequently depicted as a sun-disk, which appears on the flags of Peru and Argentina. He was married to his sister, the moon goddess Mama Killa.
Sun gods of this country's mythology include Aten, around whom Akhenaten focused a new religion, and another named Ra.
This sun goddess birthed three women from the sword of her brother, Susano-o, but angrily claimed that they belonged to Susano-o when he upstaged her by birthing five men from her necklace.

bonuses.leadin: Here comes the sun! For 10 points each, name some sun deities.

parts.text: Name this Norse god of war, the son of Odin and Frigg.
Tyr's hand was eaten by this wolf-giant-thing, the son of Loki, in order to construct a magical chain to bind him.
At Ragnarok, Tyr is destined to fight this watchdog of the underworld that guards Helheim. This creature is known for his four eyes and blood-drenched chest.

bonuses.leadin: This god is identified with the Tiwaz rune. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this ethnic group whose traditional religion worships Olorun as the king of all orishas, or minor gods.
After he turned his male children from suns into the waters of Earth, Olorun transformed his grandchildren into these creatures. The Zodiac sign Pisces represents one of these creatures.
Oduduwa became the first ruler of this legendary Yoruba city, which is considered the birthplace of humanity. Oduduwa planted a palm nut at this location that became the progenitor of nature.

bonuses.leadin: According to the creation myth of these people, the divine king Oduduwa created land by letting a five-toed chicken spread dirt around the world after his superior, Obatala, got drunk. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this agricultural tool used to separate grain which became a symbol of pharaonic power.
The flail and crook were originally symbols of this Egyptian god, the husband of Isis.
Another royal symbol in Egypt was the uraeus ("yoo-RAY-us"), one of these animals. One of these animals is found beside a vulture on the forehead of the golden mask of Tutankhamun.

bonuses.leadin: Tutankhamun holds a crook and this other object on his coffinette. For 10 points each:

parts.text: In a tragedy attributed to Aeschylus, Kratos and his silent sister Bia order Hephaestus to violently bind this second-generation Titan who stole fire from the gods.
Kratos is the son of Pallas and this goddess. For being the first immortal to give Zeus aid during the Titanomachy, her name became a binding oath for the gods.
In Aeschylus's Libation Bearers, Electra invokes Zeus, Kratos, and this goddess to support her and Orestes's goals of revenge. This goddess of justice was a second-generation Hora.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about Kratos, the divine personification of strength in Greek mythology, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Name this stock character of Russian folklore, the youngest of three sons and husband of Marya Morevna, often depicted wielding the possibly-magical Sword Kladenets.
Stories generally pit Ivan against this 'Deathless' evil wizard, who escapes Marya Morevna's dungeon after tricking Ivan into giving him twelve buckets of water. He hides his soul in an egg.

Ivan gets killed a lot: for example, he was sliced up by his brothers and revived during his quest for this mythical bird, commonly seen throughout Slavic folklore and the subject of a Stravinsky ballet.

bonuses.leadin: In one story, this figure shoots an arrow into the air to find a wife, and it is caught by a frog who just so happens to be the transformed princess Vasilisa the Wise. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this civilization to which Snorri Sturluson traces the origin of the Norse gods in his prologue to the Prose Edda. Snorri suggests that Thor's mother was the princess of a city made famous by this civilization's epics.

In another Irish-Norse parallel, Finn MacCool pierced himself with one of these weapons in order to stay awake and fight Aillen ("Allen"), while Odin pierced himself with one called Gungnir so he could discover the runes.

Mirroring an Irish myth in which Mesgegra's calcified brain became lodged in Conchobar's (KONG-koh-wer's) head, Thor had a fragment of one of these objects stuck in his head after fighting the giant Hrungnir, and sought Gróa's help to remove it.

bonuses.leadin: The Lebor Gabála states that a group of Nemedians who survived the failed assault on Tor Conaind made their way to the lands of this ancient civilization, where they became the Fir Bolg. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these edifices which can be closed to seal off the entrance to temples or other buildings. Examples of them allowed people to pass through the walls of Rome.
The Romans believed that this two-faced deity was the God of Gates. The aforementioned gate in Rome was named for him.
The Gates to the Underworld, meanwhile, were said to be guarded by this three-headed dog.

bonuses.leadin: One of these objects in Rome was closed during peacetime, and open during wartime. For 10 points each:

parts.text: The oracle of Delphi ordered this man to follow a cow and found a city at the site where it stopped; hence, he founded Thebes.
King of Thebes and husband of Jocasta, he is killed by his son, who later marries Jocasta.
Succeeding Oedipus as king of Thebes was this man, who reneged on his agreement to cede the throne after one year to his brother Polynices.

bonuses.leadin: Identify these ancient mythological Thebans for 10 points each.

parts.text: Name this process in the Egyptian afterlife, where one of the subject's organs is compared against the feather of Maat.
The weighing of the heart is overseen by this jackal-headed Egyptian god of the afterlife, who also presides over the mummification process.
Ammit, the devourer of souls, has the head of one of these reptiles, whose snout shape differentiates them from alligators.

bonuses.leadin: At the end of this process, the subject either continues to the Field of Reeds or their soul is devoured by Ammit. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Figures like Castor and Pollux, Laertes, Atalanta, and Theseus all were members of this mythical crew who sought the fleece.
Along the way, Hylas, the servant of this Argonaut, was kidnapped by water nymphs. This Argonaut searched for Hylas for a long time before returning to complete his twelve labors.
The Argonauts stopped at this city near the modern-day-country of Georgia, where Jason was aided by the king's sorceress daughter Medea in completing three tasks in exchange for the fleece.

bonuses.leadin: For ten points each, answer some questions about Jason and the quest for the Golden Fleece:

parts.text: Name this king. The Geste de Doon de Mayence deals with rebellions against this ruler, who is served by paladins like Roland.
This warrior, who wields the sword Cortana, originally fights against Charlemagne but then joins his court. This Danish warrior eventually moves to Avalon with the fairy Morgana.

After killing Charlemagne's nephew, the four sons of Aymon flee with this horse, who can adjust his size to match his riders. This horse smashes a stone around his neck and escapes when Charlemagne tries to drown him.

bonuses.leadin: To atone for unknowingly killing this ruler's son, Huon de Bordeaux is given impossible tasks like kissing the daughter of the emir of Babylon four times. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this Norse trickster god. With the giantess Angrboda ("AHNG-er-boh-dah"), this god fathered Hel, Jormungandr ("YOR-moon-gahn-dur"), and the wolf Fenrir.

One of Loki's worst acts was handing a spear of mistletoe to the blind god Hodr ("HOH-der"), who used it to kill this other god. This god of light could not be resurrected because the giantess Thokk refused to weep for him.
Loki gave birth to this eight-legged horse after seducing Svadilfari ("SVAH-dil-fah-ree"). This "greatest of all horses" is the mount of Odin.

bonuses.leadin: This god's wife Sigyn ("SIG-in") uses a bowl to prevent venom from dripping onto his face. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this mythological three-headed dog, who guarded the entrance to Hades to prevent anyone from escaping.
Whenever this mythological monster lost one of its heads, two would grow back in its place; luckily for Heracles, only the center head was immortal.
While riding Pegasus, Bellerophon was able to slay this multi-headed beast, which had heads of a snake, goat, and lion.

bonuses.leadin: Orpheus, Heracles, and Aeneas were some of the very few who were able to slip past it. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify these creatures that, in many Asian and Mesoamerican mythologies, are said to live on the moon, due to a pattern of dark patches on the moon resembling them.
According to myths of these people, the shape on the moon comes from either a rabbit being thrown in the face of the god Tecciztecatl, or from Quetzalcoatl elevating one to the heavens.
A non-lunar hare is saved from a flaying by Okuninushi, the son-in-law of this Shinto storm god who often feuds with his sister Amaterasu.

bonuses.leadin: One of these creatures is said to be the companion of Chang'e, spending its time pounding out the elixir of life with a mortar and pestle for her. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this chief god of the Greek pantheon.
Zeus's mother saved him from being eaten by this Titan, his crazy father. Zeus later overthrew him after forcing him to vomit out Poseidon and Hades.
Three of these figures had helped Cronus overthrow his father, Uranus. Their forge made Zeus' thunderbolts, helping to defeat the Titans.

bonuses.leadin: This deity fathered Persephone by Demeter, and Athena burst fully formed out of his head. For 10 points each:

parts.text: In one of his usual antics, Gonggong headbutted and destroyed Mount Buzhou. Since that mountain had been holding up the sky, this wife of Fuxi (foo-she) replaced it with the legs that she severed from the turtle Ao (ah-oh).

Yu the Great is said to have killed Gonggong's nine-headed snake minion Xiangliu (she-aang-"leo") in his quest to end these natural disasters. Yu the Great eventually succeeded in stopping these disasters through the construction of a series of channels and dams.
Yu the Great was assisted by Yinglong in his struggles against Gonggong and Xiangliu. Yinglong is one of these creatures commonly associated with rain, rivers, and the underworld in Chinese myth.

bonuses.leadin: Answer some questions about the Chinese water monster Gonggong. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this place whose creation myth is told with the Kumulipo, a chant which links royalty with the gods. In a story from this place, the goddess Hi'iaka journeys to retrieve the singer Lohiau, only to have her sacred grove burned down.

This Hawaiian goddess, who burned down Hi'iaka's sacred grove in a fit of jealousy, lends her name to volcanic glass that takes the form of thin strands. She lives in the caldera of Kilauea (key-lao-ay-uh) and represents fire, lightning, and volcanoes.

This trickster god worked with his father to push the sky upwards, freeing mankind from its oppressive weight. He also goaded his brothers into hauling the Hawaiian Islands out of the ocean with his great fish hook.

bonuses.leadin: The Four Gods, Kāne, Kū, Lono, and Kanaloa, command the religious pantheon of this place. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Give this name of two chieftains, the sons of Telamon and Oileus. One of them committed suicide after going mad and slaughtering cattle and sheep, under the impression that they were Greek generals.
This man was awarded the armor of Achilles and thus earned the ire of Ajax the Greater. He would later face a difficult journey home to Ithaca and his wife Penelope after the Trojan War.

Along with Diomedes, Odysseus stole this statue of Athena from the Trojans, believing that its theft would hasten the end of the war. It was later brought to Rome by Aeneas and kept in the Temple of Vesta.

bonuses.leadin: One man with this name was killed after boasting to Poseidon that he could not be drowned. For 10 points each:

parts.text: What kind of mythical animal represents the east? These mythical creatures are associated with rain and, inEnglish, share a name with fire-breathing lizards from European myth.
Another of the Auspicious Beasts, the Vermillion Bird, is named in English for this Greek mythical bird thatrepresents rebirth.

This other animal, representing the west, isn't commonly associated with any western mythical animal. It isoften pictured with a long neck and a horn or antlers, and is legendarily associated with giraffes.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about the Four Beasts of Chinese folk religion, which appear in legend, representthe four cardinal directions, and are important to feng shui, for ten points each.

parts.text: In a Somalian legend, humans can partly turn into what animals by rubbing themselves with a stick during the night? Roman geographers presented these real animals as monstrous 'crocotta' that could mimic human speech.

All people with this profession are believed to possess buda and transform into hyenas according to Ethiopian folk tradition. In the Kalevala, the Sampo was created by Ilmarinen, an immortal with this profession.
acceptableAnswers: prompt on inventor with “what other profession did these people have?”

parts.text: Buda is a curse believed to be caused by an "evil" one of these body parts. The wedjat depicts these body parts belonging to Ra and Horus.

bonuses.leadin: People who possess an evil force called buda are able to transform into these animals. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this hero, who accidentally caused Aegeus to commit suicide after forgetting to change his sails from black to white.
Theseus volunteered to be one of fourteen youths sent to this location to be eaten by the Minotaur. While in this location, Theseus was guided by a golden string given to him by Ariadne.
Theseus was nearly poisoned by this witch before Aegeus noticed his sandals and sword and saved him. This figure was abandoned by Jason after the search for the golden fleece.

bonuses.leadin: This hero killed Procrustes by forcing him to fit in his own bed and pushed Scirion [SKIH-REE-ON] off of his own cliff while travelling to Athens. For 10 points each--

parts.text: The Inuit god Nanook decides which hunters find and kill this predator, the largest land carnivore in the Arctic.
This canine is a trickster deity in many Native American cultures. In a Navajo myth, he created the Milky Way.
This "Confederacy" of tribes in New York observed a religion centered around longhouses.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, identify the following about Native American religions and cultures.

parts.text: Name this Egyptian god of knowledge and magic who invented writing and mediated disputes between the gods.
Thoth weighed this body part of deceased Egyptians against the feather of Ma'at to determine whether they were worthy of entering the afterlife.
Thoth stood alongside Ra as he traveled on this kind of object, which represented the sun. Horus painted one of these objects to look like it was made out of stone to win a race.

bonuses.leadin: This god of law helped judge the worthiness of the dead by weighing the feather of Ma'at. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name this deity, a myth about whom was reconstructed by the philologists Ivanov and Toporov in which this deity battles Veles, who appears as a dragon.

Several 11th to 12th century artefacts honouring Perun shaped like these weapons have been found. Along with the hammer, mace and arrow, Perun was often associated with these weapons, depicted in "hatchet amulets".

In some Slavic folk tales, Perun is also associated with these objects, which when thrown cause lightning bolts to burst from the sky. Hesiod wrote of how golden varieties of these objects were guarded by the Hesperides in Greek mythology.

bonuses.leadin: An early reference to this deity appears in Procopius' History of the Wars, which records how early Slavic tribes acknowledged "one god, creator of lightning, the only lord of all". For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this being who was buried under Etna as punishment for a conflict in which he participated along with his brothers, who included Porphyrion and Alcyoneus.
Enceladus was one of these beings, who were birthed by Ge the earth mother in order to avenge the imprisonment of her children the Titans after the Titanomachia.

This name is shared by both a giant who joined Enceladus and the others in the Gigantomachia and one of the Aloeidae, the brother of Otus, who sought to reach Olympus by piling Mount Pelion on top of Mount Ossa and then rape Hera and Artemis. They may have been the same being.

bonuses.leadin: This figure is not Typhon, but according to Apollodorus, he is buried under Mount Etna, which erupts when he moves. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this Monkey King, whose incredible memory comes from remembering every monkey on Earth. This character accompanies the monk Tang Sanzang in the Chinese epic Journey to the West.
Sun Wukong tried to steal the peaches to gain this trait. Chinese alchemists added mercury to an elixir to acquire this trait.
acceptableAnswers: any clear reference to living forever

parts.text: Sun Wukong possessed one of these objects, called Ruyi Bang, that could grow or shrink at his command. A sacred snake appears wrapped around one of these objects owned by Asclepius.

bonuses.leadin: This figure becomes trapped under a mountain for 500 years after stealing the Peaches of Heaven. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this giant who imprisoned Loki in a chest for months to get the trickster god to bring Thor unarmed into his house.
Loki obligingly got Thor to approach Geirrod without this all-powerful hammer or the strength-enhancing belt Thor used to carry it.
Luckily, Thor survived the scrape with Geirrod thanks to the advice of this god's mother Grid. This silent god will use his shoe to maul the Fenris Wolf at Ragnarok.

bonuses.leadin: This giant lost his daughters Gjalp and Greip afer their attempt to squash Thor against the ceiling only got them crushed into the foor. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this Hindu epic told by Vyasa that focuses on the Kurukshetra [koo-rook-shay-trah] war between the Kauravas [kaw-rah-vahs] and the Pandavas [pan-dah-vahs]. The Bhagavad Gita is a section of this epic work.
In the Mahabharata, this eighth avatar of the god Vishnu serves as the charioteer and companion to the Pandava prince Arjuna.

Krishna helps Arjuna marry Draupadi by giving him the opportunity to participate in a shooting contest. In the contest, Draupadi's potential husbands must shoot the eye of a moving one of these animals that swims on the ceiling, without looking at it.

bonuses.leadin: A character in this work loses his entire kingdom in a dice game. When he plays again, his entire family is forced to live in exile for twelve years. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name these objects which, according to an interpretation by Elias Lonnrot, include the Sampo that could produce gold and salt out of thin air in addition to more typical products of this object like flour.
The Sampo is forged by this legendary blacksmith from the Kalevala in an unsuccessful attempt to win the hand of the beautiful daughter of the witch queen Louhi.
One theory hypothesizes that Louhi's land of Pohjola was the land of the Sámi. Unusually shaped examples of these objects called Sieidi are held sacred by the Sámi.

bonuses.leadin: The Aarne-Thompson-Uther tale type 565 classifies tales about magical examples of these objects including the Grottasöngr where two Jotunn slave girls work in one of these objects. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this Guardian of the Cedar Forest who, after being hit with Shamash's thirteen winds, was axed to death by Enkidu and his companion.
That companion of Enkidu was this two-thirds-immortal king of Uruk, the namesake of a Sumerian epic.
Dumuzid the Fisherman reigned as king of Uruk between Gilgamesh and this man, who fathered Gilgamesh with the goddess Ninsun.

bonuses.leadin: It is claimed that this figure's "breath is fire", while his shout "has the power of a deluge", and after his death Enlil redistributed his "seven terrors" or "seven radiances". For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these objects that provide the epithet of a knight who is forced to use one after riding two horses to death in pursuit of the villain Maleagant ("MALL-ay-ah-gahnt").
This "Knight of the Cart" rescues Guinevere from Maleagant and has an affair with her in Chrétien's poem. This Knight of the Round Table was the father of Galahad.

Maleagant was eventually replaced as the main villain in the Matter of Britain by this illegitimate son of Arthur. This man exposed Guinevere and Lancelot's affair and was killed at the Battle of Camlann.

bonuses.leadin: In a Chrétien de Troyes ("CRAY-tee-yen duh TWAH") poem, a man with an epithet referring to one of the objects crosses a bridge made of swords to rescue a maiden kept in an impenetrable crystal tower. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this setting for a series of children's novels loosely based on Welsh myth.
This author wrote the Chronicles of Prydain series. His last book of the series, The High King, won the Newbery Medal in 1969.
The title object of this second book in the series is used to create an army of undead soldiers.

bonuses.leadin: Inhabitants of this land include the pig Hen Wen and the assistant pig-keeper Taran. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this god of thieves born on Mount Cyllene to the nymph Maia. That same day, this god gifted Apollo with the lyre he had created as compensation for his cattle.

Mount Cyllene is located in this region, whose namesake was also raised by Maia after their mother Callisto was turned into a bear. This region is the home of a shepherd god who created the syrinx flute from the reeds of a nymph he was pursuing.

In a local myth, Mount Cyllene's name comes from the word "crippled," referencing Hermes' dismemberment after stealing this activity invented in Arcadia. The princess Palaestra lends her name to ancient schools for this activity, deriving from her aid to Hermes in that myth.

bonuses.leadin: According to this god's Homeric Hymn, his hunger drove him to run away and eat Apollo's cattle as an infant. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this figure who wields the spear Gáe Bulg ("guy bolg"). This figure singlehandedly defeated the armies of Queen Medb ("mayv") at the Cattle Raid of Cooley.

Original language term required. Cú Chulainn is spiritually weakened after he eats a meal offered to him by an old woman, thus allowing Lugaid to kill him and breaking one of these taboos in Irish myth.
The meal the old woman offered Cú Chulainn was the meat of these animals, thus breaking the geis placed upon him. Cerberus was a three-headed one of these animals in Greek myth.

bonuses.leadin: This figure dies after being struck by three spears fashioned by Lugaid ("LOO-gid"). For 10 points each:

parts.text: Iktomi is a trickster figure that is human and this type of animal. In West Africa, the trickster hero Anansi is one of these types of animal.
This figure skeletized a scout who attempted to rape her, but then saw the good nature of his compatriot and gave him and his people knowledge of the seven sacred ceremonies and ceremonial pipe.
This is the Lakota term for the divine life force and their collective deities. This term is sometimes translated as the "Great Mystery."

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, name some figures and beliefs of the Lakota people.

parts.text: Name this god, the focus of the Enuma Elish, who supplanted Ea and Enlil as the head of the Babylonian pantheon.
Tiamat gave this item to Kingu to use aa a breastplate in his battle with Marduk, who then claimed it. This clay object is a legal document that confers authority over the universe.
This Mesopotamian god of wisdom is the son of Marduk. He rides the dragon-like mušhuššu and writes the destiny of every human on sacred tablets.

bonuses.leadin: The temple Esagila was dedicated to this deity, who was tasked with defeating Tiamat. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this deity, who had to piece her husband Osiris back together after he was torn apart by Seth.
Isis, Osiris, Seth and Nephthys were all children of Nut and this Earth god from Egyptian mythology.
After Horus was blinded by Seth, this deity poured milk into his eyes, restoring his sight. Often depicted as a cow, she was said to embody the living queen.

bonuses.leadin: After Gloria denied this goddess shelter, her scorpions attacked Gloria's child. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Along with a gourd, a Daoist figure named Li Tieguai carried one of these objects after his spirit entered the body of a homeless beggar. Li is frequently nicknamed for his use of this object
Iron Crutch Li was part of this group of figures, including Lu Dongbin. They include the gender-ambiguous Lan Caihe and live on Mount Penglai.
This fangshi of the Eight Immortals first appeared on Earth as a white bat and served as the advisor to Emperor Yao in a previous life. He also rides a donkey that he can fold up into his pocket.

bonuses.leadin: A figure nicknamed for one of these items was given a tablet by Laozi after resisting the temptation of a woman made of wood. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this location where some people were consumed by Ammit if they failed a test involving an object belonging to Ma'at.

In the test, this body part of dead Egyptians was weighed and compared to the feather of Ma'at. If this body part weighed more than the feather, they were devoured for having insufficient truth and justice.
The god Thoth also hung out in Duat. He was typically depicted as having the head of either a baboon or this other animal.

bonuses.leadin: Those that passed a test were able to pass through this location to Aaru, the Field of Reeds. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Medea is the jealous wife of this Greek hero, the leader of the Argonauts.
Medea believed that she earned a place of favor in Jason's life by helping him and his Argonauts recover this mythological relic.
Medea's story was famously told by this Greek playwright, whose other works include Orestes and Electra.

bonuses.leadin: The Greek story of the sorceress Medea has captivated readers for hundreds of generations. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This Norse goddess had a chariot pulled by two cats. It was customary to give cats to newlyweds to represent this goddess' blessings on the couple.
Freyja was not the only Norse deity to have a chariot pulled by unconventional animals: Thor's chariot was pulled by two of these animals, named Tanngrisnir and Tanngnjostr ("tong-nyo-ster").
In addition to his ravens Huginn and Muninn and the horse Sleipnir, Odin had two of these animals, named Geri and Freki.

bonuses.leadin: Animals play many roles in Norse mythology, from harbingers of doom to general annoyances. For ten points each, answer the following questions about the fylgja ("fill-juh"), or animal companions, of the gods.

parts.text: According to one story, this Biblical woman approached Tiberius Caesar and claimed that Jesus had risen. While making her plea her lunch turned red, resulting in the first Easter Egg.
This "doubting" apostle is believed to have sailed to India and established an early church there; thus Catholics venerate this Apostle as the Patron Saint of India.
This Apostle is thought to have been crucified on a namesake X-shaped cross. Another story tells that instead of being crucified he was spirited away to Scotland, where he is the patron saint.

bonuses.leadin: Identify some New Testament figures from stories that almost certainly never happened. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this figure. This figure killed his own father with a scythe and later is tricked into consuming a stone, believing it to be his son.
Cronos is the leader of this group of mythological beings. These children of Ouranos include Helios and Atlas, and they were overthrown by the Olympian gods in a namesake war.
The Titan Tethys was primarily associated with this domain. Poseidon was the main Greek god of this domain.

bonuses.leadin: Rhea saved Zeus from this figure by hiding him in Mount Ida with Amalthea. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these people who celebrated the four-month-long Makahiki festival said to be founded by Lono himself. That festival involed carrying Lono's statue clockwise around this people's' central island.

This Hawaiian trickster hero created the Hawaiian islands when he hauled them up from the deep with his fishing line. This figure also slowed down the sun by beating it with his grandmother's jawbone to give humans more time in the day to cook food.

Maui gave fire to mankind when he tricked the ancestor-heroine Mahui-ike into relinquishing part of these body parts. In Inuit myth, these digits belonging to Sedna became the world's whales and seals.

bonuses.leadin: The year of these people was divided into the time controlled by Ku, god of earth and warfare, and Lono, god of peace and cultivation. For 10 points each:

parts.text: The seahorse-like hippocampus carried the chariot of this Greek god, who was god of both the sea and horses, as well as earthquakes and storms.

Besides Poseidon, Melqart, the god of the sea and trade from this culture, also rode a hippocampus as depicted on ancient coins from his city, Tyre. Cadmus was legendarily a prince of this seafaring and mercantile culture.

Hippocampi were often conflated with the decidedly less mythical dolphin. In one story, a musician with this name was rescued by dolphins after being kidnapped by pirates. An immortal horse with this name was sired by Poseidon with Demeter.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer some questions about the hippocampus-the nautical kind:

parts.text: Hercules's 10th labor involved retrieving the red cattle guarded by this demon. This resident of Erytheia had three human heads and three sets of weapons and armor, but was ultimately defeated by a poisoned arrow.
After slaying Geryon, Hercules retrieved these fruits from the Hesperides nymphs. One of these fruits was guarded by Ladon, and was feuded over by Hera, Athena, and Aphrodite.

As his twelfth and last labor, Hercules kidnapped this three-headed guard dog of the underworld, who was supposedly so scary that Eurystheus had to hide in a large jar. Hercules wrestles and chains this creature unarmed.

bonuses.leadin: Name some stuff about the later labors of Hercules, for 10 points each:

parts.text: This Greek word is used to refer both to the realm of the dead and the brother of Zeus who rules that realm.

The Judges of the Dead decided whether souls were to enter Hades or this location, a pit below the Earth, reserved for the most evil monsters and men. Sisyphus cheated death by trapping Thanatos in this place.
This place is reserved for righteous mortals, and is more pleasant than Asphodel. Hesiod called this place "The Isle of the Blessed."

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about the Greek underworld. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this substance which is said to make up both Heimdall's teeth and the mane of his horse, as well as some fruit guarded by Idunn.

After accidentally killing Ottar, this god was forced to fill Ottar's skin with gold by way of reparation to Ottar's father Hreidmarr. This father of Hel and Fenrir also tricked Hoder into killing Baldur with a dart made of mistletoe.

That reparation consisted of the gold Loki had extorted from this dwarf after capturing him in Ran's net. This figure was also forced to give up a namesake ring that could produce gold, on which he laid a curse in revenge.

bonuses.leadin: Freya, the Norse goddess of love, cried tears of this substance after the disappearance and probable death of her husband Od. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this precious metal that also describes a "Fleece" sought by another Greek hero, Jason.
This Greek hero asked Atlas to retrieve the golden apples of the Hesperides for him after he was ordered tocollect them by King Eurystheus.
Heracles is sometimes considered a member of this group of heroes, who sought the Golden Fleece in anamesake ship.

bonuses.leadin: The Hesperides guarded apples made of this substance, but gave some to their father, Atlas, on the requestof a Greek hero. For ten points each,

parts.text: Name this part of the body from which Tefnut is born. An adze is applied to this part of the body in an Egyptian ceremony to restore the senses of the deceased.
The god who opens the mouth in that ceremony is this creator worshipped at Memphis. The bull Apis is an aspect of this non-Osiris god of craftsmen, who fathers Nefertem with his consort Sekhmet.

Purification during the ceremony is undertaken by the astronomical god Dwn-'nwy, who is identified with this constellated son of Thyria and Apollo. He shares his name with a Trojan son of Poseidon who was raised by seagulls.

bonuses.leadin: A kuchisake-onna has this part of her body mutilated while a futakuchi-onna has an extra one on the back of her head. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this third play in Aeschylus's Oresteia trilogy.
This mother of Orestes was murdered after she killed her husband Agamemnon and had an affair with Aegisthus. Her ghost rouses the Eumenides at the opening of the play.
This goddess, the daughter of Zeus, casts the deciding vote to acquit Orestes. Her symbol is the owl, and she was a virginal goddess of wisdom.

bonuses.leadin: This play's chorus is made up of the title figures, who hunt Orestes for murdering his mother. For 10 points each:

parts.text: In Greek mythology, death comes from the jar opened by this first woman, who was formed out of clay by Hephaestus.
In Polynesian mythology, death results from the failure of this culture hero's quest for immortality, which is foiled by the laughter of a bird. He also creates the Hawaiian Islands using a jawbone.
The killing of Maui by the underworld goddess Hine-nui-te-po is one myth involving this dangerous body part, whose common appearance in myth may reflect a fear of castration.
acceptableAnswers: accept anything about a vagina with teeth

bonuses.leadin: Answer some questions about myths about the origin of death, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Using forms such as a court trial and a jump rope rhyme, twelve hanged maids interrupt Penelope's experience during The Odyssey in The Penelopiad by this Canadian author of Cat's Eye and The Handmaid's Tale.

In this author's Ragnarok: The End of the Gods, a child evacuated from the Blitz reads a book of Norse myth. She also wrote about the relationship of Randolph Ash and Christabel LaMotte in Possession.

This author's Dream Angus contains several modern and one archaic story about a Celtic god who is turned into a swan. He created the Botswanan investigator Precious Ramotswe for The No. 1 Ladies' Detective Agency series.

bonuses.leadin: Name some things about the Canongate Myth series, in which contemporary authors were recruited to rewrite old myths, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Name this Egyptian god of the underworld who was chopped into 14 pieces that had to be recovered by Nephthys.
Osiris' wife was this goddess of fertility who assembled the pieces of Osiris' body and discovered the secret name of Ra.
Osiris' body had been chopped up by this brother of his and god of chaos. This god famously feuded with his newphew Horus, who tricked him into trying to sail a raft made of stone.

bonuses.leadin: He is usually depicted holding a crook and flail. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this domain of a god who abducted Oreithyia (oh-ray-THEE-uh) and brought her back to Thrace.
Zephyrus, the god of the West Wind, was the father of Xanthus (ZANTH-uss) and Balius, two of these creatures noted for their extreme speed. These animals form the lower body of centaurs.
Zephyrus is sometimes given as the father of this legendarily-swift horse, who is more commonly held to be the offspring of Poseidon and Demeter.

bonuses.leadin: One god of this domain sired two sons, Calais (kuh-LAY-iss) and Zetes, who went on to sprout golden wings. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This god replaced his cupbearer Hebe with Ganymede, whom he had abducted in the form of an eagle.
This goddess of dawn ended up with a cicada for a husband after granting Tithonus of Troy immortality but forgetting to also give him eternal youth.
After killing her husband Priam and son Astyanax, this Greek kidnapped Andromache, though that was more as a spoil of war than as a lover. This man was also known as Pyrrhus.

bonuses.leadin: Poor Trojans! The gods keep on kidnapping them for lovers. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this Norse goddess, the wife of Thor. During a series of insults in the Poetic Edda, Loki accuses this deity of having an affair with him.
Sif's headpiece was crafted by this group of dwarves, whose other crafts include Odin's spear Gungnir and Frey's ship Skidbladnir.

Loki bet his own head that the Sons of Ivaldi were better crafters than the dwarf Eitri, but lost the bet when Eitri crafted some objects for the gods including Mjolnir, one of these weapons, for Thor.

bonuses.leadin: After Loki cut off this goddess' hair as a prank, her husband demands that Loki swear to get her a golden headpiece to replace it. For 10 points each:
